_meta.source: Derived from FAA MMEL Boeing B-737 Rev 62 (2022-11-28) covering -100/-200/-300/-400/-500/-600/-700/-800/-900/-900ER, plus FAA MMEL B-737 MAX Rev 6 (Draft 2024-04-23). Item IDs follow ATA 4-digit + sub-item convention. Both MMELs share the same ATA taxonomy as A32x — only the system implementation, terminology, and certain item counts differ.

categories.A: No standard repair interval. Operator must specify (often 1-3 days or by flight cycles).
categories.B: 3 consecutive calendar days, excluding day of discovery.
categories.C: 10 consecutive calendar days, excluding day of discovery.
categories.D: 120 consecutive calendar days, excluding day of discovery.

_meta.totalItemsInRealMmel: FAA MMEL B-737 Rev 62 contains approx. 1300-1500 individual items across 30+ ATA chapters (full doc ~750 pages, larger than A320 due to multi-variant coverage from -100 through -900ER). MAX MMEL Rev 6 adds ~200 MAX-specific items.

differencesVsA32x.hydraulics: B737 uses System A / System B / Standby (engine-driven pumps + electric motor pumps + air-driven pump on B). A32x uses Green/Yellow/Blue with PTU. Different MEL items entirely under ATA 29.
differencesVsA32x.flightControls: B737 uses cable-and-hydraulic conventional flight controls (no fly-by-wire on NG; MAX adds fly-by-wire spoilers only). No ELAC/SEC/FAC; instead FCC (Flight Control Computer) for autopilot only. MEL items under 27 are simpler in number but each item has wider operational impact.
differencesVsA32x.engineControl: B737 uses FADEC (CFM56-7B EEC and LEAP-1B EEC) — same dual-channel concept as A320 CFM56-5B / LEAP-1A.
differencesVsA32x.pneumatic: B737 has high/low stage bleed valves per engine + PRSOV + crossbleed; uses 8th and 5th stage tap on CFM56-7B. A32x uses HP/IP valves and precoolers similarly but bleed scheduling differs.
differencesVsA32x.apu: B737 NG uses APS 2000 / GTCP85 (older) or APS3200-similar variants per fleet; B737 MAX uses APS 5000-class. A32x uses Honeywell 131-9A.
differencesVsA32x.fuel: B737 has 2 wing tanks + 1 center tank, no NGS on early NG (FRM mandated post-SFAR 88), no integrated ATA 47 chapter for older airframes.
differencesVsA32x.avionics: No IMA/AFDX. Uses ARINC 429 federated avionics with CDS (Common Display System). No ATA 42/45/46 inventory comparable to A320 NEO IMA cabinets.
differencesVsA32x.fbwLaws: No alternate/direct law transitions (NG only). MEL-relevant for SMYD (Stall Management Yaw Damper) instead of FAC.
differencesVsA32x.mcas: MAX-only: MCAS-related dispatch impacts under updated AOA disagree alerting.
differencesVsA32x.doorPlug: MAX 9 mid-exit door plug — post-2024 inspection regime under AD 2024-02-51.

_meta.note: Sample below curates 87 representative items used to seed the WO template generator. Real MMEL has finer granularity (per-channel, per-side variants, per-fleet variant table).

One of two recirc fans inoperative; both packs must operate.
Single AP channel inoperative; CAT II/III autoland NOT authorized depending on configuration.
Inoperative provided manual thrust procedures briefed; performance penalty per OM-B.
One channel inoperative; speed restriction may apply.
One VHF inoperative provided remaining VHF radios serviceable; B737 NG typically equipped with VHF L/C/R.
Inoperative provided not required by route (oceanic/remote operations).
Inoperative provided VHF voice comms operate; CPDLC requirements per route.
Inoperative provided FDR operates normally.

Inoperative provided AC standby bus available from normal sources.
